_README: THE HAND VERDICT ON ALL 26 lone-quarter-in-2/4 bars of the shared record (Beethoven 5 / Litolff 984073, pdf pp.1-4). Each row is one CROP that was looked at against the print, at 34 px per staff space, on a contact sheet that also carried 5 glyphs the record itself calls restWhole and 5 it calls a notehead, drawn identically, as controls. Where the panel was not decisive on its own the whole printed staff was rendered as a strip and the bar compared with its own neighbours -- the only fair control for a bar, since it is the same part, the same plate and the same ink.

_verdicts.whole_rest: the page prints a WHOLE REST here and the detector called it a notehead. Sean's observation, exactly.
_verdicts.notehead: the page prints a real note here. The bar is underfull because the REST OF ITS MUSIC was not read, not because this note was invented. Deleting it would delete real music.
_verdicts.junk: the page prints neither -- the box sits on a slur apex, or on the junction of a stem and a staff line. A spurious detection, but not this fault.

_what_is_NOT_established: That the 18 'notehead' rows carry the right PITCH or the right DURATION. The verdict is only that ink of that kind stands there.
n = 1 document, 1 publisher, 4 pages of ~16, on the low-res bitonal end of the corpus.
The adjudication is one reader's (this session's), against the print, not Sean's.
